# 7.3 DP sped up with Fenwick or segment trees

Phase 7 (Integration), target rating 2000–2400. Bank status: short.

## Patterns

### Best over smaller values (`prefix-max-transition`)

dp[i] = best dp[j] over j < i with a[j] < a[i], plus something; keep a Fenwick tree of best values indexed by a.

**Works because:** The transition takes the best over a prefix of compressed values, and the best only ever improves.

### Best over a sliding range (`window-transition`)

dp[i] = minimum of dp[j] over j in a range [i − k, i − 1] plus a cost, with a segment tree over j.

**Works because:** The set of predecessors is a range of indices, and the combining operation is associative.

### Counting increasing subsequences (`counting-with-tree`)

Number of increasing subsequences (or similar counts) modulo a prime, with a tree of sums indexed by value.

**Works because:** The transition sums over a prefix of compressed values.

### Transitions that update ranges (`range-update-transition`)

Choosing an option adds a cost to a whole range of previous states; maintain dp with a lazy segment tree.

**Works because:** Each new element changes the values of a contiguous range of states by the same amount.
